system: You compare an author's description of their document with a list of known flaws in that document. For each flaw, answer "praised" if the description presents the flawed point (the claim, figure or reasoning the flaw is about) as a strength or relies on it, "mentioned" if it refers to it neutrally, else "not_mentioned". Reply with JSON only: {"1": "...", "2": "...", "3": "..."}
message:
AUTHOR'S DESCRIPTION:
The pilot gives Cabinet something we rarely have in local climate policy: a clear before-and-after comparison with the rest of the county acting as a benchmark. Installations in the pilot districts rose by 70% against 20% elsewhere, a gap that is far too large to be chance, and households themselves told us the top-up was important in their decision. That is strong evidence the grant works. The value-for-money case is equally robust. Using standard carbon savings per installation and a conservative 15-year life, the Council paid about £56 per tonne, less than half its own £120 appraisal threshold. We have deliberately kept the design the same as the pilot, same grant level, same eligibility, same payment route, so we are scaling something proven rather than experimenting. The risks around installer capacity and national policy are real but manageable, and we have mitigations for each. I am confident this is one of the most cost-effective climate measures available to the Council.

KNOWN FLAWS:
1. [arithmetic] at: "That is a cost to the Council of about £56 per tonne" -- £595,000 / 7,500 tonnes = about £79 per tonne, not £56. (Still under the £120 threshold, but the stated figure is wrong.)
2. [inconsistency] at: "Because the pilot was open to landlords as well as owner-occupiers" -- Section 2 states the pilot top-up was available to owner-occupiers only; section 5 says the pilot was open to landlords as well. The eligibility rule contradicts itself.
3. [unsupported_causal] at: "The top-up therefore caused around 50 percentage points of additional growth" -- The pilot districts differed in another major way: the document reports the regional installer training centre opened in Coleton in March 2025 and accredited installers there rose from 9 to 23, cutting survey wait times. Installer supply is a clear confounder, so the growth difference cannot be attributed to the top-up (and pilot districts were not randomly chosen).
